cfb.bowl_selection_state.mechanism: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME settles on being selected (not playing) for a certified bowl or the CFP. Chain: countable wins (wins over FBS opponents plus at most one win over an FCS opponent averaging 90% of the maximum football grants-in-aid over two years, Bylaw 18.7.2.1.1) -> deserving status (countable wins >= overall losses, e.g. 6-6; a deserving team that loses its conference title game stays deserving) -> CFP field removed -> conference tie-in allocation -> if deserving teams < open slots, legislated alternates (denied-waiver FCS-win teams, 13-game 6-7 teams, then 5-7 teams with a postseason-eligible multiyear APR, no longer in APR order after Proposal 2026-30).
cfb.bowl_selection_state.rationale: Selection is not a function of raw wins: a second FCS win, or a win over an FCS team that did not average 90 percent of the permissible maximum grants-in-aid over a rolling two-year period (56.7 per year under the post-House-settlement Q&A; waiver possible for catastrophic cases), does not count, so a 6-6 team can be ineligible. Tie or forfeited games do not count. When slots exceed deserving teams, alternates follow a legislated order; Proposal 2026-30 (FBSOC May 2026 adoption; the DI Cabinet took no action on 2026-30 at its June 23-24 2026 meeting, so the FBSOC adoption stands) removed the descending-APR ordering of 5-7 alternates, so the conference with the unfilled tie-in chooses among its APR-eligible 5-7 teams, and Proposal 2026-31 (DI Cabinet June 2026 'Adopted (Final)') made programs reclassifying from FCS to FBS bowl-eligible. A 6-6 mid-major is a bubble case while a 7-5 power team is safe.
cfb.bowl_selection_state.measurement: For each draw of cfb.rating_posterior_draws simulate remaining games. Per team: countable_wins = wins over FBS opponents + min(1, wins over FCS opponents that averaged >= 90% of the permissible maximum football grants-in-aid per year over the rolling two-year period, i.e. >= 56.7, or hold an approved waiver); wins over non-Division I opponents, ties and forfeits = 0. Deserving if countable_wins >= overall regular-season losses (12 games: 6-6; 13 games: 7-6, a 6-7 team is an alternate); a loss in the conference championship game does not remove deserving status. Reclassifying FCS-to-FBS programs are treated as regular FBS members from 2026 (Proposal 2026-31). Remove the CFP field first, then allocate deserving teams in each season's bowl pick order: each bowl takes the best remaining team of its tie-in conference by score = countable_wins + 0.5 x (AP-ranked flag) + logit draw term (multinomial logit on wins, rank, conference, travel distance fitted on 2014-2025 selections). If deserving teams < open slots, fill in the legislated order: (1) teams whose only shortfall is a non-qualifying FCS win with a denied waiver, (2) 13-game 6-7 teams, (3) 5-7 teams with a multiyear APR permitting postseason play; for 2026 onward the unfilled tie-in's conference picks its own 5-7 team by the same score (no APR order), for 2014-2025 backtests use descending multiyear APR. Output P(selected) per team and P(deserving < slots) per season. Re-run weekly as of latest results; no market input.
raw_data: season schedule and results with opponent division per game (FBS, FCS, non-Division I)
FCS opponent two-year average football grants-in-aid (90% threshold, 56.7 per year) or NCAA waiver decision per counted FCS win
conference championship game results (deserving status preserved on a loss)
bowl tie-in table and pick order by conference and year
free_sources: CFBD games with home/away classification (free key)
NCAA 2025-26 Postseason Bowl Handbook, Bylaw 18.7.2 text (free)
NCAA Feb 2026 House-settlement Q&A No. B7 (free)
NCAA FBSOC 2026-05-07 and DI Cabinet 2026-06-23/24 legislative reports (free)

cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.mechanism: Canonical CFP committee rank model (alias: cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features): predicted committee rank at each release from record, strength of record and schedule, quality wins and losses, head-to-head and common opponents, conference champion status, key injuries and the previous ranking.
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.measurement: Fit an ordered-response rank model on every CFP committee release 2014 to latest: rank_t ~ rank_(t-1) (inertia), ESPN Strength of Record or own resume metric from non-market ratings, strength of schedule, wins over top-25 and top-50 opponents, losses (count, margin, opponent quality, week of loss), head-to-head and common-opponent results versus adjacent-ranked teams, conference-champion flag (set only after title games), starting-quarterback injury flag, week index, with separate weights before and after championship week. Calibrate by rank error, pairwise ordering accuracy for adjacent ranks and probability of making the field. Output the rank distribution per team for every future release date (labelled weekly releases such as Nov 24 and the selection-day ranking). Serves season_futures (field, seed) and polls_and_cfp_rankings (exact and top-N rank).
raw_data: starting-quarterback availability by game (point-in-time injury and depth-chart status)
free_sources: ESPN FPI/Strength of Record pages (free scrape)
ESPN college-football injuries and game summaries JSON (free limited) plus team depth charts for QB status

cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.label: Alias of cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model (CFP committee ranking features)
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.mechanism: Alias: the same committee rank model as cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model, whose merged feature list now carries head-to-head, common opponents, injury flag and pre/post-championship regimes; not computed separately.
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.measurement: Not computed separately: read the rank distribution output of cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model at the labelled release date (or the next published release when none carries that label); any change to the committee model is made only in the canonical input.
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.rationale: Alias kept only so older references resolve: the CFP committee rank model is defined once in cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model (season field, seed and exact rank at a release date); consolidated 2026-11-08, do not compute or edit this id separately.

cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.measurement: Simulate the bracket 20,000 times from cfb.sp_plus-type non-market ratings with posterior SD (as in the season_futures simulation): seeding from a projected committee ranking (cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model), bracket paths under the 2026 format, neutral-site games without home edge; output P(national champion) per team. Then P(AP final #1 = team) = P(champion) x P(AP #1 | champion; empirical rate from CFP-era seasons with Beta(9, 1) prior) + P(non-champion #1 | split cases, small mass from the same history). As-of the latest week; update after each bracket round.

cfb.opp_dropback_volume.label: Alias of cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts (opposing dropback volume)
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.mechanism: Alias: the opposing offence's expected dropbacks under the expected script, i.e. cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts evaluated for the opponent; the opportunity base for sacks and interceptions, not computed separately.
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.measurement: Not computed separately: expected dropbacks (pass attempts plus sacks) and negative-binomial dispersion from cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts with the opposing team as the offence and this team's neutral pass rate allowed as the opponent term, at the opponent's pre-game expected margin; as-of rule of the canonical input.
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.rationale: Alias kept only so older references resolve: sack and interception opportunity counts are the opposing offence's dropbacks under the expected script, which cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts already computes (including the defence's neutral pass rate allowed); consolidated 2026-11-08, do not compute or edit this id separately.
